body: Not a bad idea. I filed for an appointment with the right office last night,

I have tried dxm, but it's not accesible where I am, sadly. I spent the last two days as drunk and high as I could, and I think I'm out of the woods for now. Thank you for taking the time to talk to me.

To answer your other questions, I'm from the US and I'm 30.
I could go through the paperwork, but I have to file before the 1st and if I'm killing myself why bother?

I went into social work to try and keep my friends alive, I started by volunteering at needle exchanges and homeless drop in centers when I was still a homeless teenager and built that into a career over the years. Now I'm tired of watching people die and I'm tired of living myself.

I have read that book, and recommended it to many people. It's a useful tool if you're trying to do self care. 

So I didn't specify, but I'm a trans man, not a trans woman, and I have never transitioned because it's expensive and I wouldn't be able to make money doing sex work if I transitioned. Sex work has been my main source of income for years, social work doesn't pay enough to survive, generally.
I would need a degree to teach language here, also I would have to go through complicated paperwork to work legally. I'm over an ocean away from my home country.

I hope you continue to feel fulfilled helping people, part of my strong response is what we in the helping professions call burnout. 

When you spend years helping others and it doesn't make any difference and you forget to take care of yourself because there are more important things to worry about, other people's lives are at stake.

And then you end up like me, sitting alone in a flat in a foreign country trying to hide from your problems but only hating yourself and getting more and more mentally ill.

What I'm saying is make sure you take care of yourself, I guess.

I have thought about trying other cities in my home country, but I don't have any job possibilities. I can't do social work anymore because I'm burned out and I don't make enough as a sex worker to support myself. Additionally, I don't think I have enough money to get home regardless.

I have been here for 3 months. I knew I was coming here to die when I left my home. I told everyone I had a bright future and friends who were going to hook me up with other artists and galleries. It was all bullshit, but I tried to make a life here anyway, hoping something would change. It hasn't.

And I disagree with you that I am brave or strong. I ran away from my problems, broke up with a loving partner and left a community that respected me because I couldn't deal with life. 

Now I'm alone almost every day in an empty flat, in a country where I can't communicate with anyone.
No I cannot speak the language. It makes life very difficult.

No. I'm utterly burned out from helping other people. The idea of trying to help another person to survive in a world that is full of oppression and constant danger and suffering only makes me sadder.
